description: Every day for three years, a spark has flashed across the dark sky of my mind. I am Efrem Gelaye, a collector of ideas: platforms, theories, and inventions. I study at Wolaita Liqa School and Excelle Center, train with Ethiocoders Initiative, and lead the team Andromeda Researching and Coding. I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to work with NASA through the Space Apps Challenge, where my sparks can finally meet the stars. I dream of turning all my ideas into beacons that guide others.
summary:
Download X is a file-sharing project created by Team Nigat from Addis Ababa, led by Efrem Gelaye, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.  
​The Problem: Internet access is often slow, costly, or missing, making it difficult to share large files like maps and mission data—a challenge also faced by network-less space missions.  
​The Solution & How It Works: Download X connects two computers directly to transfer any file across any distance without mobile data, Wi-Fi, or a router. Inspired by Xender and quantum entanglement, the system uses a tiny one-time handshake requiring only 1–5% of a normal download's data, after which the file transfer needs no data at all.  
​Steps:
​1. Install Download X on both computers.  
​2. Pair them using a short code.  
​3. Choose a file on the sender's computer.  
​4. The receiver gets it instantly.  
​Impact: This tool cuts data costs for students and rural communities, enables teams to share large NASA datasets in areas with weak internet, and widens access to STEM learning in Ethiopia and beyond.
